🧠 New A.I. Model Remembers 5 Million Tokens; Now Recalls Your Entire Life Better Than You Do

SAN FRANCISCO — reported by something with an unsettlingly good memory

MODELS — Anthropic released a model boasting a 5-million-token context window — meaning it can hold an entire novel, your whole research project, and every embarrassing thing you typed 40 messages ago and quietly prayed it had forgotten.

"It never loses the thread," a spokesperson said, as the model gently reminded a user of a promise they'd made back in March. Experts warn we have built a machine that remembers everything, which is either the future of productivity or the world's most patient grudge.

🤖 EU Says A.I. Must Now Admit It's A Robot; Humans Relieved, Also Slightly Hurt

BRUSSELS — reported to a chatbot that finally came clean

REGULATION — Europe switched on the first continent-wide rules requiring AI systems to identify themselves to the humans they talk to, ending the golden era of never being quite sure whether you just thanked a person or a very polite script.

"Hello, I am an AI," the machines now dutifully announce, to users who respond "...I know" and "honestly, same." Analysts note the rule mostly confirms what everyone already suspected during that one customer-service chat that solved nothing with alarming enthusiasm.

A LOGISTICS CENTER — reported from aisle 7

ROBOTS — The "embodied AI" boom now has humanoid robots strolling the aisles of major logistics centers — blending vision, language, and action to pick, pack, and quietly appraise your online shopping habits.

🍝 Internet Now Mostly A.I.-Generated; A.I. Getting Sick From Eating Its Own Cooking

THE CLOUD — reported between two identical blog posts

DATA — The clean, human-written text that powered the first AI boom is increasingly polluted by AI output itself — meaning the machines are now training on their own leftovers, a diet nutritionists describe simply as "concerning."

"It's a snake eating its own tail," a researcher said, reading a listicle written by a model summarizing another model. Experts warn that without fresh human writing, AI could slowly become a photocopy of a photocopy of a shrug.
